series.license: CC BY (HDX: World Bank DECDG Real Time Prices)
series.notes: World Bank Real Time Prices, field exchange_rate_unofficial, median of the 28 market rows per month. Cross-check against the D1 daily rate series.

series.label: LBP per USD, official (BDL) rate, monthly regime value
series.notes: Regime table, not a market series, aligned with D1 fx_official_monthly (FAOSTAT): 1,507.5 (peg) to Jan 2023; 15,000 from 1 Feb 2023 to Jan 2024 (including Jul-Dec 2023); 89,500 from 31 Jan 2024. series.label: Generator tariff, ministry table last column (reads as LBP per kWh)
series.notes: Ministry generator table, last column, whose printed header is "number of cut hours per month". The values scale with the diesel reference (Jun 2026 41,973 with diesel 2,061,450; Jan 2017 302 with diesel 14,906), so they read as an LBP per kWh tariff, but the header and a press report disagree: L'Orient Today gives 48,241 LBP/kWh for Aug 2025 against 30,309 in this column (29 Aug 2025). HYPOTHESIS: LBP per kWh; the discrepancy may be a second tariff band (altitude or metering). Treat as unverified and compare gen_kwh_press_lbp.

series.label: Generator kWh tariff as quoted in press (ministry tariff)
series.notes: Press-quoted ministry tariffs: Jul 2022 13,545 (The961 summary), Aug 2022 13,796 (The961, 1 Sep 2022), Jul 2023 31,870 (Waradana), Aug 2025 48,241 or USD 0.54 (L'Orient Today summary). Sparse: the ministry's own monthly list for 2019-2024 is blank in the fixed-fee columns. Sources are secondary; verify against the ministry gazette before quoting.

series.label: Generator fixed fee 5 A, USD at market rate
series.notes: Derived: ministry fixed fee / monthly median market rate. 385,000 LBP is about USD 4.3 at 89,500; the operators' real all-in bills are much higher once the metered kWh is added.

series.label: Private-sector minimum monthly wage (decree level), LBP
series.notes: Step series: each point is the month a decree level took effect (or was adopted, see below) and the value holds until the next point. Decree basis per point: 1996-07: Decree 8733 of 8 Jul 1996 (cited in the text of Decree 7426/2012; amount per UNHCR labour-sector paper and Executive Magazine Nov 2008). Value before 1996 not sourced. || 2008-09: Cabinet decision Sept 2008 (Executive Magazine, Nov 2008: law finalised 10 Sep 2008, private-sector application from Nov 2008, retroactive to May for the +200,000 general raise). Decree number not retrieved; the month shown is the decision month. || 2012-01: Decree 7426 of 25 Jan 2012 (cited in Decree 11226/2023; amount per UNHCR labour-sector paper and L'Orient Today 21 Jul 2025). An Oct 2011 cabinet deal for LBP 700,000 for lower earners is reported by Executive Magazine; the decree set the minimum at 675,000. || 2022-04: Decree 9129 of 12 May 2022: +1,325,000 cost-of-living allowance on the 675,000 minimum, effective 1 Apr 2022 (MTV Lebanon text of the decree; Beirut.com). || 2022-10: Decree 10598 of 19 Oct 2022: +600,000 added to the monthly wage (Lebanese University legal database; the961 15 Jun 2022 on the Index Committee agreement). Effective date within 2022 not retrieved; the month shown is the decree month. || 2023-04: Decree 11226 of 18 Apr 2023, in force with Official Gazette no. 17 of 26 Apr 2023 (Mercans payroll alert; L'Orient Today 18 Apr 2023). Decree 11343 of 29 May 2023 amended it; its effect on the minimum was not retrieved. || 2024-04: Decree 13164 of 5 Apr 2024 (Lebanese University legal database); Index Committee decision of 19 Mar 2024 (Credit Libanais note). Effective date not retrieved; month shown is the decree month. || 2025-08: Decree 699 published in Official Gazette no. 32 on 24 Jul 2025, effective 1 Aug 2025; daily wage LBP 1,300,000 (Aldic notice, WageIndicator; L'Orient Today 21 Jul 2025 for the signature). No change as of 30 Sep 2026: the Index Committee was still discussing a new minimum (MTV Lebanon, 28-30 Sep 2026). Daily-wage workers have a separate minimum (LBP 1,300,000 per day from Aug 2025). GAP: nothing sourced before 1996. The public-sector minimum stayed at LBP 675,000 (about USD 7.5), IMF TA report 26/19 (Mar 2026). Sources: Primary: https://data.unhcr.org/en/documents/download/69776 ; http://77.42.251.205/Law.aspx?lawId=302301 (Decree 10598) ; http://77.42.251.205/Law.aspx?lawId=330147 (Decree 13164) ; https://www.aldic.net/en/ministry-of-labor-decree-699-dated-24-july-2025-increasing-the-minimum-monthly-basic-salary/

series.label: Private minimum wage in USD at the official rate, monthly
series.notes: Derived: decree level / official rate of fx_lbp_usd_official_monthly (1,507.5 peg to Jan 2023, 15,000 Feb-Jun 2023, 15,000 Jul-Dec 2023, 89,500 from Jan 2024). The USD 448 pre-crisis figure is this series; after Oct 2019 it overstates what the wage bought because the official rate was not the rate people transacted at. Use the market series for purchasing power. CORRECTION 2026-10-02 (V2 verification): Jul-Dec 2023 previously used the Sayrafa platform rate (85,500 / 89,500, USD 105 / 101); now at the official 15,000 (USD 600), so the jump to 89,500 falls in 2024-01, not 2023-12.

series.label: Public administration pay as a multiple of the pre-crisis base salary (civil servants, cumulative)
series.notes: Cumulative multiplier on the base salary (scale of Law 46/2017) for active public-administration staff, not including the fuel-canister, perseverance and transport allowances. 2022-11: x3 = base + two supplementary salaries under law 10 of 15 Nov 2022 (L'Orient Today 18 Apr 2023 says staff had received "two basic salaries since the start of the year", so the effective month may be Jan 2023: low confidence on the month). 2023-05: x7 after Decree 11227 of 18 Apr 2023 (+4 salaries, 14 days attendance a month, effective 1 May 2023; L'Orient Today, NNA). 2023-12: x9, +2 for active administration (+3 for retirees and the security forces), decided 28 Feb 2024, retroactive to 1 Dec 2023 (Nowlebanon, LIMS, Annahar). 2024-12: x13 reported "by end of 2024" (Al-Akhbar 22 Jan 2026) and "current multiplier of 13" (Kataeb, 2025); the decision date of the step from 9 to 13 was NOT retrieved, so this point is reported (📣), not verified. 2026-03: +6 provisional salaries decided by cabinet on 16 Feb 2026 (decision no. 2) from 1 Mar 2026, capped at LBP 50 million a month, so 13 + 6 = 19 on paper; on 27 Jul 2026 the finance minister sent a draft decree spreading the six over 12 months to Aug 2027 and unions contested it (L'Orient Today 1 Aug 2026), so the amount actually paid in 2026 is lower than 19. The government line is to reach x30 (50% of 2019 value) from 1 Jan 2027 (Daily Beirut, 18 May 2026). The military and retirees follow different multipliers (x3 supplements in 2024, see SIGMA 2025).
